NFL NBA MLB NHL NCAAB NCAAF Contests Home Streak Survivor King of Covers My Contests Century Casinos Considers Selling Alberta Assets Century Casinos is considering sales of Canadian properties and its Casinos Poland stake. According to Century Casinos Co-CEO Peter Hoetzinger, the Colorado-based operator is weighing sales of its Canadian properties and its majority interest in Casinos Poland as its strategic review moves toward possible asset disposals. Key Takeaways Century Casinos is considering sales of Canadian properties and its Casinos Poland stake. Potential Alberta sales could split racinos and commercial casinos, while buyer interest exists for both. Selling Canada and Poland assets would leave Century focused on seven casinos across five U.S. states. In a second-quarter earnings call on Friday, Century Casinos' boss updated investors on the potential future of the company’s four properties in Alberta: two commercial casinos and two racinos. Hoetzinger discussed how those assets could be sold together or divided into two packages, with the racinos grouped separately from the commercial casinos. Interest exists in both structures, and Century expects it may be able to disclose progress on at least one package before year-end. The company also told investors it is exploring a sale of its stake in Casinos Poland. Two unidentified groups are conducting due diligence on the business, although the process faces added complications from Poland's regulatory environment and the war in neighboring Ukraine. Century has not indicated that either prospective buyer has an advantage. Selling both operations would sharply narrow Century's geographic footprint. The company would be left with seven U.S. casinos, including properties in Colorado, Missouri, Maryland, Nevada and West Virginia. The review comes as Century looks for ways to reduce debt and improve shareholder value. Management has said it wants greater clarity on potential asset sales before making significant debt-reduction commitments. Poland has become a particular pressure point. The business has generated weaker earnings than before the pandemic and has drawn attention from investors seeking portfolio changes. Century's shares have also fallen 91% over the past five years, increasing pressure on management to produce a clearer path forward. Century posts record Q2 revenue The possible asset sales come as Century reported record second-quarter net operating revenue and adjusted EBITDAR, supported by stronger North American results. Net operating revenue reached $152 million for the three months ending June 30, up 1% from a year earlier. Earnings from operations rose 4% to $17.2 million, while adjusted EBITDAR increased 5% to $31.7 million. The company's net loss attributable to shareholders dropped to $10.9 million from $12.3 million. Performance varied sharply by region. U.S. Midwest revenue increased 8% to $44.7 million, while U.S. West revenue climbed 16% to $23.4 million. Adjusted EBITDAR in the U.S. West segment jumped 93% to $4.5 million, driven by improved results at the Nugget Casino Resort in Nevada. Canada also improved. Revenue rose 2% to $20.4m, while adjusted EBITDAR increased 11% to $6.2 million. Poland moved in the opposite direction. Revenue fell 19% to $19.9 million, while adjusted EBITDAR dropped 97% to just $52,000. The segment posted an operating loss of $659,000 after generating a $464,000 operating profit a year earlier. For the first six months of 2026, consolidated revenue rose 3% to $289.2 million. Adjusted EBITDAR increased 12% to $56.6 million, while the shareholder net loss narrowed 17% to $27.4 million. Century Casinos closed June with $60.2 million in cash and cash equivalents and $336.5 million in outstanding debt. It also carried a $708 million long-term financing obligation tied to its master lease with VICI Properties subsidiaries. Hoetzinger said during the call that the company is awaiting more clarity on the sell of assets before it will commit to debt-reduction measures. https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/26451307.ips.text: Ipswich Crown Court Court Ipswich men jailed after violent town centre attack By Abigail Banks-Smith Reporter Share 0 Comments 2 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Two Ipswich men have been jailed for over seven years after a town centre attack which left a man with a fractured skull, shattered eye sockets and lasting vision problems. Egidijus Abramavicius, 34, of Grange Road, and Aurimas Kazmiruk, 39, of Jeffries Road, were unanimously convicted by a jury of causing grievous bodily harm with intent following an assault in Ipswich town centre on April 5, 2024. Ipswich Crown Court heard the pair acted together against the victim, repeatedly punching and kicking him during an attack that began outside an Ipswich convenience store and continued into an alleyway beyond CCTV coverage. Both men were sentenced on August 10 at Ipswich Crown Court, despite only Abramavicius being in attendance. (Image: Charlotte Bond) His Honour Judge David Wilson said the victim was left “to fend with two males on his own” before running towards his home in an attempt to "escape the violence". When the assault ended, he suffered from multiple wounds to the back of his head, bleeding around his nose and mouth, missing dentures and bruising to both arms. Hospital examinations revealed severe injuries, including numerous facial fractures that have permanently altered his vision. In a victim personal statement, he said the assault continued to affect his daily life. He told the court: “I now have glasses that I have to use for reading.” He said he experiences headaches every evening and described the pain as feeling “like my head will explode”. The victim added that he no longer goes out alone at night and fears retaliation from the defendants or their associates. Describing the incident as “gratuitous violence” aggravated by alcohol consumption, Judge Wilson sentenced both men to seven-and-a-half years' imprisonment. However, Abramavicius faced further convictions passed on from Carlisle Crown Court which brought his total sentence up to eight years. Both men were made subject to restraining orders preventing contact with the victim. Ipswich Crown Court Court Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... Now with The Witcher IV on the way, seeing Geralt pass down the mantle to surrogate daughter, Ciri, as well as the launch of the third and final The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt DLC, Songs of the Past , the future is looking bright for fans of the beloved RPG series. That being said, there is still some time to wait until these major releases, but this is the perfect thing to keep you occupied in the meantime. The Witcher 3: The Last Wish is a stunning mod for the hit CD Projekt RED title that aims to bring The Witcher book series to life more than ever. What many people forget, is that before it was an award-winning video game series, The Witcher franchise began its life as a book series by author Andrzej Sapkowski. It was way back in 1986 that the character of Geralt of Rivia was first introduced after Sapkowski won a short story contest and then, in 1993, The Last Wish was first published in Polish, before finally being translated to English in 2007. Whilst the video game series has taken inspiration from the original source material, it is not an exact copy, but The Witcher 3: The Last Wish aims to change that. As the creators say, " The Last Wish Project is a fan-made, non-commercial video game recreation of the original Sapkowski book "The Last Wish", which aims to recreate the original stories into playable quests and interactive worlds to explore in REDengine 3." "As Mr. Sapkowski once wrote, life can be as sad as a cow headed for slaughter. I hope this non-commercial project cheers you up. Many things felt visually the most present in the first Witcher, and the first game remains a strong artistic inspiration for the project in many aspects. The Last Wish Project is designed as an action adventure." With the alpha version of The Last Wish now available to download courtesy of Nexus Mods, players can expect "a fully playable recreation of the original Witcher book with a true devotion to the source material" and with over 2,000 downloads, it is safe to say that this The Witcher 3 mod is already a major hit with fans. https://www.dw.com/en/us-china-ai-race-d.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5N2R5 US President Donald Trump has announced a change of course in his AI policy Image: Manuel Balce Ceneta/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Developers warning against their own technologies and a government unwilling to take action — that was the situation in the first half of September amid concerns in the US that AI models were becoming too powerful. Several developers and decision-makers from major AI companies had also called for slowing down the development of the technology . In response, US President Donald Trump posted one of his typical all-caps tweets on his social media platform Truth Social: "AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX." Trump also asked "Concerning AI, when, in the History of Business, did anyone see the Leaders of an Industry call for Regulation that, if strongly implemented, will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy?" Against this backdrop, it comes as something of a surprise that Trump announced over the weekend — following yet another tirade about various alleged Democratic scams — that he would establish an "AI Force" and appoint a special envoy to address the issue. What exactly did Trump say? In his post, Trump promised that he would by no means slow down the industry's growth. "However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System," he wrote. "To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI 'Czar' — Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!" he added. Trump left open exactly what the individual's duties and powers would be and what resources would be allocated to the position. Trump's announcement could be an attempt to undermine an initiative by California's Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom. The previous day, Newsom had announced plans to establish a commission to regulate Silicon Valley-based tech companies. Among other things, Newsom wants to require these companies to build an emergency shut-off switch into their programs, which would allow humans to stop AI agents that have spun out of control. Several states, including some led by Republicans, are pushing for regulation. US fear of China's dominance The current "AI race" between the US and China is often compared to the space race between the US and the former Soviet Union in the 1960s. Several US companies are currently considered industry leaders. To ensure this remains the case, Trump intends to continue giving them free rein. However, this is not just about economic interests. There is concern that Chinese dominance in artificial intelligence could also lead to Beijing's rise as the sole superpower. In a widely discussed essay , Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, not only warned of the consequences of continued unchecked AI development; he also outlined the potential consequences of the AI competition between the US and China. "If we greatly restrain our AI capabilities in the belief that China will do the same, and then China defects, AI could be so powerful that such a defection could lead to their geopolitical dominance. Therefore any agreement must either have ironclad verifiability, or must be limited enough that defection would not be militarily existential," Amodei wrote. Tech leaders call for transparency and an emergency switch off for robots and AI technologies Image: Tingshu Wang/REUTERS Does China regulate AI? In China, technological developments have traditionally been much more closely tied to governmental objectives. As early as 2017, the State Council of China issued a development plan for a new generation of artificial intelligence. Another strategy paper sets out milestones through which China aims to achieve global dominance in the field of AI by 2030. The regulations are primarily enforced by the Chinese Cyberspace Administration (CAC), which also issues licenses. Regulation in China ensures that AI models do not run counter to official political doctrine. For example, the Chinese AI chatbot DeepSeek consistently provides answers loyal to the regime when asked politically sensitive questions — such as those regarding Taiwan , the Tiananmen Square massacre , or the oppression of the Uyghurs — as DW previously documented. The underlying logic of Chinese regulation is thus based on the question: How does an AI system align with state objectives? This represents a clear distinction from the risk-based regulation envisaged, for example, by the European AI Act and now being called for in the US. Could the US and China share information on AI technology as discussed between US Minister of Finance Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng? Image: Bai Xueqi/Xinhua/dpa/picture alliance Is an AI agreement between the US and China imminent? On Thursday, Trump will host Chinese President Xi Jinping at a state dinner at the White House. The topic of AI is likely to be very high on the agenda. The US already proposed establishing a mechanism for exchanging information about serious risks posed by AI . The proposal was discussed at a meeting between Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday in New York. "We think that, just like with any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and the number two AI powers in the world is very important," Bessent said. Whether they actually decide to act on this will likely be left up to the two presidents. After all, for them, potential transparency obligations regarding AI are by no means the only point of contention in the negotiations. For years, trade restrictions on high-performance AI chips and rare earth elements have been a recurring issue and the extension of a basic trade agreement is also on the agenda. Whether mutual trust is strong enough to lead to reciprocal concessions on AI will likely only become clear at the meeting. This article was originally published in German. Photograph: Rungroj Yongrit/EPA Andrew Bailey Bank of England governor walks out of IMF summit in protest against Russia Andrew Bailey among finance leaders to leave session in Bangkok when Russian finance minister addressed group Harry Taylor Sat 17 Oct 2026 08.15 EDT Last modified on Sat 17 Oct 2026 08.17 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The Bank of England governor, Andrew Bailey, has taken part in a walkout of finance leaders who left an International Monetary Fund meeting in protest against Russian involvement. Bailey joined counterparts from France, Germany and a number of Scandinavian and Baltic countries who left the session in Bangkok when the Russian finance minister, Anton Siluanov, addressed the group in Russian. The Bank of England confirmed that Bailey took part. The president of the German Bundesbank, Joachim Nagel, said nearly half of all delegates took part in the joint departure when Siluanov started speaking. “The Ukraine war is existential for us in Europe,” one European diplomat told the Reuters news agency. “We cannot normalise relations with Russia.” The walkout was acknowledged by the chair of the IMF’s steering committee, the Saudi finance minister, Mohammed al-Jadaan. Al-Jadaan said: “We came here for a reason, and we achieved ⁠it. Look at this chair statement, it clearly says that all members agreed to the statement, so that’s what matters.” Germany had warned against efforts to bring Russia back on to the international stage. Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers this year. The US has been supportive, with the treasury undersecretary Erin Browne telling Reuters that Washington supported Russia’s presence despite concerns from European countries. The meeting in the Thai capital heard that the global economy was showing remarkable resilience despite the war between Russia and Ukraine, and in spite of the issues around the strait of Hormuz caused by the US’s bombing campaign. However, al-Jadaan added that there was no room for complacency, amid public debt levels and high bond market rates. A statement from al-Jadaan after the IMF meeting said: “The global economy has weathered the latest in a series of shocks better than expected, but buffers have been eroded, and resilience cannot be taken for granted.” He added: “Escalating conflicts and trade tensions could further disrupt critical trade routes, exacerbate commodity price pressures, including in refined energy products, and worsen energy and food security.” Explore more on these topics Andrew Bailey Bank of England International Monetary Fund (IMF) Russia Foreign policy Ukraine Europe news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.portfolio.hu/gazdasag/202611.text: A Boston Consulting Group (BCG) által 2020 és 2024 között készített elemzések jelentős költségvetési ráfordítással születtek meg. Az előző kormányzat éveken keresztül elzárta a nyilvánosság elől a dokumentumokat, amelyek közül négyet "Bizalmas" minősítéssel látott el. A most közzétett, bárki által szabadon hozzáférhető anyagok rávilágítanak arra, hogy a korábbi döntéshozók már évekkel ezelőtt is pontosan tisztában voltak az ágazat kritikus állapotával. A tanulmányokból kiderül, hogy az Orbán-kormány legkésőbb 2020-ban részletes képet kapott az egészségügy súlyos problémáiról, így az orvos- és szakdolgozóhiányról, a kórházak eladósodásáról, valamint az ellátáshoz való hozzáférés zavarairól. Átfogó választ mégsem adott rájuk" - írja a Hegedűs Zsolt vezette minisztérium. Az idő múlásával a tanulmányokban megfogalmazott javaslatok egy része elavulttá vált, ezért a minisztérium a jelenlegi szakmai munkáját már nem ezekre a dokumentumokra építi. A közzététel célja elsősorban az átláthatóság biztosítása volt, amint azt a tárca is hangsúlyozta, miszerint "azért tesszük közzé őket, mert a közpénzből készült, mindenkit érintő elemzések megismerése a társadalom joga." A magyar egészségügy átfogó átalakítását célzó, sokáig titokban tartott tanulmányt 2020. május 12-én rendelte meg a Belügyminisztérium a Boston Consulting Group (BCG) nemzetközi tanácsadó cégtől , nettó 277 millió forintért, vagyis áfával együtt mintegy 352 millió forint közpénzből. A dokumentum már 2020 augusztusára elkészült, és az egészségügyi ellátórendszer stratégiai átalakítására, a működési problémák kezelésére, az intézményrendszer és az egészségügyi humánerőforrás átszervezésére fogalmazott meg javaslatokat. Az előző kormány azonban már 2020 augusztusában egyértelművé tette, hogy a tanulmányt nem hozza nyilvánosságra: a Belügyminisztérium arra hivatkozott, hogy az a kormányzati döntések előkészítését szolgáló adatokat tartalmaz, amelyek nyilvánossága az információszabadságról szóló törvény alapján a keletkezésüktől számított tíz évig korlátozható. A dokumentum így 2030-ig maradhatott elzárva a nyilvánosságtól. A titkolózás mögött szakpolitikai megfontolások is kirajzolódtak: a BCG projektvezetője, Újlaki Ákos később arról beszélt, hogy az egészségügyben jelen lévő erős érdekcsoportok már a kezdeti szakaszban megakadályozhatnák az érdekeiket sértő reformot. Újlaki Ákos többször is részt vett előadóként a Portfolio által szervezett Private Health Forum konferencián. A tanulmány nyilvánosságra hozataláért a K-Monitor korrupcióellenes civil szervezet indított pereket, arra hivatkozva, hogy a közpénzből készült, a teljes társadalmat érintő egészségügyi reformot megalapozó dokumentum megismerése közérdek, és az átalakításokról érdemi társadalmi, illetve szakmai vitát kellene folytatni. A szervezet előbb a BCG-t, majd a Belügyminisztériumot is perelte, változó bírósági eredményekkel. A 2023 októberében született elsőfokú ítélet még a minisztériumnak adott igazat, 2024 januárjában azonban a Fővárosi Ítélőtábla már a dokumentum kiadására kötelezte a tárcát, mert nem találta kellően megalapozottnak a nyilvánosság korlátozásának indokait. A Belügyminisztérium ezt a döntést is megtámadta, és végül 2024 júniusában a Kúria kimondta, hogy nem köteles kiadni a tanulmányt.
